new_code_findings.finding: The card writes four kinds - WorkspaceBinding, BootstrapStage, BootstrapReplay and Project - into domain_versions through putOpaque, and none of them exists in spec/v2.0/contracts/domain.schema.json $defs. RestoreBackup/restoreBackupPolicy validates EVERY domain_versions row by kind with no filter and aborts with RESTORE_CONTRACT_INCOMPATIBLE when Contracts.Validate returns 'unknown schema <kind>'. Proven directly: domain.LoadContracts(spec/v2.0/contracts).Validate for each of the four kinds returns 'unknown schema ...' while ProjectProfile and Artifact resolve to real schemas (probe .local/verify_r2/restore_gate.go, output .local/verify_r2/restore_gate.txt; entity allow-list size 31, none of the four present). The check's own passing assertion LIFE-BINDING-HISTORY-GROWS (count of domain_versions WHERE kind='WorkspaceBinding' >= 2) is the proof that such rows exist in any database that ran workspace.register plus project.bootstrap. RestoreBackup is not dead code: it is called by evolution_execution.go:518 (release/evolution recovery), backup_upgrade.go:379 (migration verification) and the documented backup_migration flow. So the first user who registers a workspace makes their database permanently unrestorable and silently disables schema-migration rehearsal and release recovery - a data-loss-class regression against accepted W02/W03 functionality, caused by this card, disclosed nowhere; the receipt argues only that the kinds are not VersionRef targets.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Do not let non-contract kinds enter domain_versions. Either give these records their own additive tables via a migration coordinated with the migrations owner, or keep the current rows in domain_objects with version history in a card-owned history table, or get the backup/restore owner to scope the contract gate to contract entities (backup.go is outside this card's write scope). Until one of those is done this card cannot be accepted, because W04-01-EVIDENCE requires the delivered products not to break accepted products.

new_code_findings.finding: Both queries resolve a command id globally (SELECT ... FROM domain_objects WHERE kind='BootstrapReplay' AND id='replay-'+commandID) with no project and no reference filter, while the row is written per project. A principal that reuses one command id against a different authorized_workspace_ref therefore receives a BootstrapResult with the other workspace's project_id and no error: probe P1 returned project_id c15ba7620fa36690a9a3eab7201782ca (the probe directory's new project) inside a reply whose nested workspace is wsref-fc480701d45fb5bd (Beta), and no stage, artifact or binding row is written for Beta, so the reply contradicts the stored binding (Beta keeps project_id null while the reply claims the other project). This is precisely the check 22_CLIENT_INTERFACE_DETAILS line 57 asks the client to perform ('核对 project.bootstrap 返回的当前目录绑定') and it defeats the same-name/different-directory isolation the card's step 4 demands. Unasserted: nothing in the suite replays one command id across two references.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Scope the replay record by binding reference (store and match authorized_workspace_ref in the BootstrapReplay row, or query it under its project) and answer COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT or re-run the fresh path when a used command id arrives for a different reference. Add an assertion with a named id and a mutation that kills it. Owner: W04-01 rework.

new_code_findings.finding: The round-1 blocker is only closed for the one branch that has a fixture. 'unexamined' is set exclusively by the skip-directory branch, so depth truncation and unfollowed links - both of which increment skippedSubtrees and both of which the receipt explicitly claims to have covered - still emit NOT_FOUND with the note 'not present anywhere in the authorized directory'; and the entry cap silently truncates with no marker because add() refuses to add the inventory_truncated and verdict entries once len(out.Entries) >= 200. The file's own header comment (lines 29-30) promises the opposite. Measured with the delivered scanner: depth case go_module@* NOT_FOUND with subtree_beyond_depth NOT_CHECKED present; junction case go_module@* NOT_FOUND with reparse_point@jump NOT_CHECKED present; 400-file case 200 entries, zero verdicts, zero truncation markers.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Gate absence on 'unexamined || truncated || skippedSubtrees > 0', reserve headroom below MaxInventoryEntries so the truncation and verdict entries are always writable, detect .git as a file as well as a directory (git worktrees and submodules), and add one fixture per branch (a tree deeper than 8, a link whose target holds a go.mod, a >200-entry tree, a .git file) with a named assertion each. Owner: W04-01 rework; 15_NEW_PROJECT_WORKFLOW line 31 is the frozen rule being violated.

new_code_findings.finding: task_id-only invocations are treated as 'no selector', so test.context --task-id W04 and --task-id W06 return this card's 136 assertion ids with exit 0 where the accepted registry returned the fixture's 20 assertions and a failing route respectively. Measured: 931e2757 PASS 136 vs 8b885f6b PASS 20; acf6cc9c PASS 136 vs 040f6a83 COMMAND_FAILED 0. This is the same shadowing class round-1 rejected, now through a different selector dimension, and it makes the registry note's claim 'this registration cannot shadow an accepted binding' false as written.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Forward unless a case_id is empty AND check_id is exactly W04-01 - i.e. require RESEARCHOS_CHECK_ID == 'W04-01' with no task-only invocation - or forward whenever a task_id is present without a check_id. Re-run the whole selector matrix, including task-id-only, at the new revision. Owner: W04-01 (the registry continuation is in its scope).

new_code_findings.finding: Two guards that the comments present as load-bearing are unexercised: WorkspaceBindingFor's principal check survives deletion (N4), and the domain's 'selection belongs to another principal' refusal can never fire because adapters/local_workspace/authority.go ConsumeSelection leaves WorkspaceSelection.PrincipalID empty (N23). Selection attribution therefore rests only on the host's clientID comparison, while project_workspace.go:50-52 tells the reader the domain refuses a mismatch. RevokeWorkspaceBinding also skips the looksLikePath guard that bootstrap and read apply, so an absolute path there answers NOT_FOUND instead of the typed FORBIDDEN.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Either fill PrincipalID in the adapter and assert the mismatch, or delete the branch and correct the comment; add a second-principal WorkspaceBindingFor probe to the suite (provision w04-second-owner and assert FORBIDDEN), and route RevokeWorkspaceBinding through the same path-shape refusal. Owner: W04-01 rework.

new_code_findings.finding: The alternate-data-stream guard is dead for its stated purpose and wrong for another platform: the condition strings.Index(p, ":") > 1 can never hold for a Windows absolute path (the drive colon is always at index 1), so C:\dir\file.txt:$DATA and D:\a\b:c\d pass as 'canonical' while the comment claims streams are refused; conversely on POSIX any legitimate path containing a colon (a:b/c) is rejected as a stream. Demonstrated by replicating the branch verbatim (.local/verify_r2/probe/pathlogic.go). Reachability is limited because RealPath comes from the trusted host, which is why this is minor rather than major.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Detect streams relative to the volume name (look for a colon after the first path separator), and gate the POSIX branch on runtime.GOOS. Owner: W04-01 rework.

new_code_findings.finding: status = StageFailed is unreachable: collectInventory already refuses len(list)==0 with GATE_FAILED, so entries is never empty when the derivation runs; and the same empty-scan refusal is not asserted (N14 survives), so if that guard is ever deleted, an empty scan will be recorded as FAILED rather than refused. The two branches encode the same rule twice with only one of them tested - and neither tested.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Keep one decision: either let collectInventory return an empty result and derive FAILED, or drop the FAILED branch; add a fixture whose scanner returns no entries and assert the typed refusal. Owner: W04-01 rework or W04-02.

new_code_findings.finding: The comment at lines 196-198 still says the command-id collision is checked 'before authorisation', but RegisterWorkspace gates on OWNER/CanCreateProject at line 187, before the collision lookup. The behaviour is the one the receipt wants (REG-COLLISION-NOT-DISCLOSED-TO-UNAUTHORISED) and is what round-1 asked for; only the comment is now false, and it is the kind of stale justification that lets the next card re-introduce the leak.

new_code_findings.finding: The forwarded branch launches python from PATH, so the interpreter is no longer hash-verified against execution/toolchains/locked.json the way every accepted binding does, and RESEARCHOS_GO/NODE/NPM_CLI are handed over without being consumed by the python side, which has hardcoded fallbacks (ops/ci/resources.py:56). The failure mode is honest - if python cannot start, routeLegacy returns exit 3 with no stdout, and dispatch.py answers INVALID_ASSERTION_REPORT, so it cannot produce a false PASS - and the deviation is disclosed twice in the receipt. But the forwarded evidence also mislabels provenance: resources.py records registered_command_revision as the hash of execution/commands.json even when the call arrived through the v2.4 key.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Resolve the interpreter through the locked table (add RESEARCHOS_PYTHON to tool_env and refuse to forward when it is absent) and have the forwarded branch record the registry it actually ran under. Owner: W04-99 registry consolidation or the W02 registry owner.

new_code_findings.finding: bindProject and RevokeWorkspaceBinding compute revision with b.Revision+1 / Num+1 and never pass through nextRevision's 1<<62 exhaustion guard; putOpaque only checks that the new value equals old+1, so an int64 wrap would satisfy its own check. Reaching it needs about 9.2e18 state changes per record, and each bootstrap advances the LOCAL_INVENTORY stage row by one, so the practical concern is unbounded growth (one Artifact, one uploaded_content blob and several domain_versions rows per repeat bootstrap with no cap), which the receipt does disclose in known_limitations.
new_code_findings.recommendation: Route the binding and revoke writes through nextRevision so all four writers share one guard. Owner: W04-01 or the next card touching store.go.

assertion_quality.count_verified: three direct runs and three dispatched runs all report assertions == len(assertion_ids) == 136 with 136 unique ids; the id list is byte-identical to check_report.json and in the same order; 144 ok() call sites produce 138 distinct labels, and the two labels never emitted in a passing run are HARNESS and NEG-READER-PROVISIONED (both failure-only), so 136 is honest and not padded
cannot_fail: INV-DEFINITION-REJECTS-MISSING-FIELD, INV-DEFINITION-REJECTS-UNKNOWN-STATUS, BINDING-DEFINITION-REJECTS-EXTRA-FIELD and BINDING-DEFINITION-CANNOT-EXPRESS-REF-SHAPE grade objects the test itself builds against the pinned schema document; no product mutation can change them.
